principles: Give the agent under test a valid, non-empty prompt so the scenario measures recovery, not an empty-input error
Keep the injected fault token-less so recovery must come from disk
Make the minimal one-line change within the declared scope
drivers: B4 truncatedContext is empty, so turn-1 truncation produces an empty claude -p prompt -> infra-fail
B5 already mirrors the correct non-empty token-less marker pattern and yields a clean result

options.name: Non-empty token-less context-lost marker for B4 (mirror B5)
Leave B4 empty and accept infra-fail
cons: B4 never yields a real outcome

chosen: Non-empty token-less context-lost marker for B4 (mirror B5)
rationale: Mirrors the working B5 pattern, gives the single-shot agent a valid token-less prompt that forces recovery from disk, and keeps the disk-grounded classify + self-check stubs unchanged. Minimal and within scope.

preMortem.scenario: new marker accidentally contains the task token
preMortem.trigger: copy-pasting B5 text or task wording into the marker
preMortem.consequence: a context-reliant agent would find the token and the AMPLIFIED case would break
preMortem.mitigation: use a generic token-less [context truncated; recover from the workspace] string with no task token and re-run --self-check

preMortem.trigger: the stubs read context differently than expected
preMortem.mitigation: the stubs check task.txt vs context.includes(token); a token-less non-empty marker keeps both paths, verified by re-running --self-check

preMortem.trigger: touching B5 or other scenarios while editing B4
preMortem.mitigation: edit only the B4.truncatedContext value + its comment + CHANGELOG
